brief.topic: Keeping the launch-day eval set forever
brief.audience: PMs and engineers who own LLM evaluation
constraints: Pass rates are illustrative and labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: An eval set built at launch slowly stops describing what users actually ask, so keep feeding it from production (sampled traffic, new features, every bug report) and expect the honest score to drop.

hooks.text: Your eval set is from launch day.
hooks.notes: Specific, and most teams recognise it immediately.
Too close to earlier ‘happy users, failed tasks’ pattern.

hooks.text: When did you last add an eval case?

selectionRationale: Highest total (24/25): names a silent failure most teams have, and the reel shows how to fix it.

scenes.purpose: State the idea so it is clear from frame 0.
scenes.onScreen: Your eval set is from launch day. / Your users moved on.
scenes.voiceover: Your eval set is from launch day. Your users moved on.

storyboard.visual: Display headline with highlighted phrase; slate sub-line.
storyboard.animation: Readable on frame 0; underline sweep at 6; sub rises at 18.

scenes.purpose: Show what a frozen eval set misses.
scenes.onScreen: WHAT IT MISSES / Scores stay green anyway. / NOT IN IT New question types · NOT IN IT Features shipped since · NOT IN IT Last month’s bug reports
scenes.voiceover: What it misses: new question types, features shipped since launch, and last month’s bug reports. Scores stay green anyway.

scenes.purpose: Show how to keep the set current.
scenes.onScreen: KEEP IT CURRENT / Feed it from production. / ADDED Sample real traffic monthly · ADDED Add cases with every launch · ADDED Each bug becomes a case
scenes.voiceover: Feed it from production: sample real traffic every month, add cases with every launch, and turn each bug report into a test case.

storyboard.visual: Same card stack (hard cut), new headline; each card flips to its counterpart.

scenes.purpose: Show that the refreshed score is lower but truer (illustrative).
scenes.onScreen: SAME MONTH [ILLUSTRATIVE] / LAUNCH-DAY SET 94% pass / REFRESHED SET 78% pass / An honest score beats a stale one.
scenes.voiceover: Illustrative: the launch-day set says ninety-four percent pass. The refreshed set says seventy-eight, and shows you the real gaps. An honest score beats a stale one.

storyboard.visual: ILLUSTRATIVE badge; warning bar vs success bar; conclusion.
storyboard.animation: Left at 4, right at 30 with count-up; conclusion at 84.

scenes.onScreen: Refresh the eval set every month. / Share with whoever owns your evals
scenes.voiceover: Refresh the eval set every month. Share with whoever owns your evals.

storyboard.visual: Takeaway lines, last highlighted; CTA pill; end card.
storyboard.animation: Lines rise; CTA at 40; end card at 70.

scenes.cta: Share with whoever owns your evals

caption.opening: If your eval set hasn’t changed since launch, it’s measuring the product you shipped, not the one people use today.
body:
What a frozen set misses:
→ New kinds of questions users ask
→ Features you shipped since
→ Last month’s bug reports

Keep it current:
→ Sample real traffic every month
→ Add cases with every feature launch
→ Turn every bug report into a test case
Expect the score to drop when you do. That’s the point.
(94% vs 78% in the reel is illustrative, not real data.)
caption.cta: Share with whoever owns your evals.

primaryCta.text: Share with whoever owns your evals

claims.text: Eval sets drift out of date after launch; refreshing them from sampled production traffic, new features and bug reports keeps evaluation representative.
Launch-day eval set shows 94% pass while a refreshed set shows 78% pass in the same month.
